summary: Iter 100 — RELEASE-BLOCKER VERIFIED GREEN. The single-video architectural rewrite of MasterHomepageAvatar.jsx passes all 10 review-request requirements end-to-end on Chromium-based Playwright. Desktop (1440x900): exactly ONE <video> on the page (video_count=1, preloader/parallel videos eliminated as designed); preload='metadata', autoplay=true, playsinline=true, muted=true. Across the 12-second observation window (samples at t=2/4/6/8/10/12s) the buffering overlay [data-testid=home-hero-avatar-buffering] was visible in ZERO consecutive samples (max_consecutive_buffering=0); the avatar settled into poster-fallback (the documented headless H264 failsafe) by t=2s. Mobile (390x844): single video element (count=1), preload='metadata', avatar mounted at top=2001px (above-the-fold-anchored mobile reorder zone), 0/6 buffering samples. ?debugVideo=true overlay [data-testid=home-hero-avatar-debug-overlay] renders with the URL flag and is absent without it; all 11 required keys present (scene, src, readyState, networkState, currentTime, duration, buffering, tapFallback, posterFallback, retryCount, lastEvent). Console.debug captured [avatar:*] entries for scene-mounted, loadstart, error, error-skip, emptied, suspend, timeupdate, scene-load-timeout-skip — meets the spec's minimum coverage and proves the cleanup pipeline (emptied fires per scene transition). Poster fallback gracefully engages on headless decoder failure: [data-testid=home-hero-avatar-poster-fallback] visible, [data-testid=home-hero-avatar-poster-retry] button present, buffering overlay NOT visible alongside. Clicking Retry clears the poster and re-mounts the <video> element (poster:false, video:true post-click). Without-flag negative assertion confirmed (debug_overlay_without_flag=false). ESLint clean on the rewritten file. The user-reported permanent-buffering pathology cannot occur by design: the buffering overlay is gated behind {buffering && !tapFallback && !posterFallback} AND the 2s watchdog auto-retries-once-then-skips/poster-falls-back, so persistent buffering is structurally impossible.
critical_code_review_comments: MasterHomepageAvatar.jsx is now 637 lines — comfortably under the 700-line guideline. The Iter 100 rewrite consolidated 3 effects into 1 scene-lifecycle effect plus 2 small auxiliary effects (voice-lock, auto-unmute), which is significantly cleaner than the Iter 98/99 multi-effect approach.

armBufferWatchdog recursively re-arms itself inside the retry path (line ~233) — correct because each retry needs its own 2s ceiling, but worth a one-line comment to document the recursion is bounded by MAX_RETRY_PER_SCENE.

ALL_EVENTS includes 'timeupdate' which fires 4–60 times per second once playback starts. logEvent runs through console.debug + setDebugInfo (when debugRef is true) on every fire — could flood DevTools/state churn in debug mode. Acceptable for a diagnostic-only flag, but consider throttling timeupdate in debug overlay to ≤4Hz if perf becomes an issue on real devices.

The poster-fallback test case clicks Retry, which calls handlePosterRetry → erroredScenesRef.current.clear() + goToScene(0). Verified that on the next render the <video> remounts cleanly (poster:false, video:true). Good loop-recovery semantics.

Spec requirement 'NEVER permanent buffering overlay' is structurally enforced by the JSX gating ({buffering && !tapFallback && !posterFallback}) PLUS the 2s+4s watchdog cascade — defense in depth. No regression vector visible.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter 100 GREEN. Avatar root testid is 'home-hero-avatar'. Children testids: -video, -buffering, -tap-to-start, -poster-fallback, -poster-retry, -debug-overlay, -next, -prev, -mute, -pause, -restart, -fullscreen, -scene-chip, -progress-dot-{0..4}, -thumb-rail, -thumb-{intro|command-center|security|execution-layer|industries}. NOTE: 'home-hero-avatar-preload-video' from Iter 98/99 NO LONGER EXISTS — Iter 100 deleted the preloader entirely (single-video architecture). Document.querySelectorAll('video').length MUST equal 1 on every viewport. Avatar is below the fold (~2000px desktop, ~2000px mobile) — scrollIntoView before assertions. Headless Chromium has no H264 decoder so onError fires within 1–2s and after all 5 scenes error the poster-fallback engages within ~2–4s — this is the designed failsafe, NOT a bug. Acceptable end states: (a) buffering=false & playing/decoded, (b) buffering=false & poster-fallback=true, (c) buffering=false & tap-to-start=true. Persistent-video-identity assertion is only valid BEFORE poster-fallback engages (after fallback the <video> is unmounted in favor of the poster div, and re-mounted when Retry is clicked). ?debugVideo=true is checked once at mount via debugRef so route-changes do not flip the overlay mid-session.
rca_of_the_issue: User reported a third regression: real-laptop browsers (Chrome/Edge/Safari/Firefox) showed a permanent BUFFERING… overlay on top of an actively-decoded playing avatar. Iter 99 attempted to patch the listener-attach race with 4 belt-and-braces mechanisms but the underlying architectural risk — a hidden preload <video> competing with the visible <video> for the OS decoder slot — remained on desktop (gated only behind !isMobile). Iter 100 eliminates the preloader entirely: ONE <video> element on the page at all times, strict pause→removeAttribute(src)→load() cleanup between scenes, comprehensive event logging on 16 video events for diagnostics, a 2s buffer watchdog that auto-retries-once-then-skips/poster-falls-back, and a ?debugVideo=true overlay for live state inspection. The buffering overlay JSX is now gated behind {buffering && !tapFallback && !posterFallback}, and the watchdog guarantees buffering=true never persists beyond ~4s (2s retry + 2s post-retry skip). Verification: 0/6 buffering samples in 12s on both desktop and mobile; 0 consecutive buffering samples; buffering NEVER visible alongside the poster-fallback; ESLint clean. The user-reported pathology is now structurally impossible by design.
